packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; packets 02 and 14 completed by further fresh readers after a display cap hid images, packet 17 reread by a fresh reader
text:
PACKET-19 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / CONDUCT
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this fragment was in my context.
- The images themselves carry modern pencil shelfmark labels: "Stams, STA, Frg. 155r" (image-002, recto) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 155v" (image-008, verso). I record them as visible labels only; they do not identify the work.
- Beyond the rules: to see the faint text better I made contrast-enhanced, rotated and enlarged copies of the packet images (Python/PIL, written to my session scratchpad). I opened no other files and used no search or reference tools.

IMAGES
- image-001: overview, face labelled 155r (reduced).
- image-002..005: native-resolution tiles of 155r (002 top left, 003 top right, 004 bottom left, 005 bottom right; they overlap).
- image-006: overview, face labelled 155v (reduced).
- image-007..010: tiles of 155v (007 top left, 008 top right, 009 bottom left, 010 bottom right; they overlap).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- A single parchment leaf, roughly square (about 14 x 14 cm going by the scale), with damage: a large lens-shaped hole near the centre, small wormholes, a lost/torn lower-left corner on 155r, modern tissue repairs on 155v (left edge), and a fold or crease line across the leaf.
- There are two layers of writing in different orientations:
  (A) 155r, top third: 3 full lines and part of a 4th (cut at the top edge) in a dark-brown, fairly cursive late-medieval/early-modern German documentary hand (bastarda/cursive), with flourished capitals. Below it are large calligraphic strapwork flourishes: long descending loops from "J" and "ß/s" ascenders, a big "S"-shaped scroll, and a paraph or flourish after the final word. To me this reads as the end of a German-language charter (sealing clause and dating line). That is an interpretation from wording and layout.
  (B) An older, faded text in grey ink, a small upright book hand with abbreviations. On 155r it runs perpendicular to the German lines (it appears as vertical columns of letters in the lower half: images 001, 002 bottom, 004, 005). On 155v it runs horizontally across the lower two-thirds (images 006, 008-010). Both sides are badly abraded and the ink has largely flaked. A small red trace sits at the left of one verso line (image-008 ~line at y 910; image-009 top), possibly a rubric or initial remnant.
  (C) 155v, upper right: a 2-3 line note in a later, darker cursive hand (dorsal or archival note?), written over the faded older text area.
- I cannot see column structure for layer B: the leaf is cut down and only line portions survive. No running titles visible.

SELECTED AREAS
1. German charter lines on 155r (images 002/003): fully read below.
2. Later note on 155v (image-008): read tentatively.
3. Older faded text (layer B): only isolated words/letters recoverable; most remains unread.

=== 1. 155r, German text (layer A) ===
Physical lines counted from the top of the image. 002 and 003 overlap in the middle (the words "absen"/"gehanngen"/"...drey...igisten" appear on both). Below, the left part is from 002 and the continuation from 003.

image-002 l.1 / image-003 l.1: [cut at top edge: only descenders and lower halves of letters; illegible]
image-002 l.2: behalt(e)r? ist? . Doc? der Heinuß? absen(n)? .
image-003 l.2 (continues): [absen(n)] . Vnnd wanns? dyser brief
   -> joined: "behalt[..] ist . Vor?/Doc? der [H/Z]einuß? absen . Vnnd wanns? dyser brief"
   Notes: first word "behalter"/"behalten" uncertain; "Doc" might be "Vor"/"Vnd"; the word after "der" begins with a looped H- or Z-like capital, then "einuß"/"ennuß"; "absen" maybe with a final flourish (absenn?). "dyser brief" fairly clear (y with descender, "brief" with long f).
image-002 l.3: 5 [margin, cut] Conuent? Innsigel hieran gehanngen
image-003 l.3 (continues): [...gehanngen] , Beschehen an
   -> joined: "...Conuent Innsigel hieran gehanngen , Beschehen an"
   Notes: first word "Conuent"/"Conuennt" (minims ambiguous: "Cauuent"). "Innsigel" with long s. "hieran" begins with a looped h. "Beschehen" with a large flourished B.
image-002 l.4: [..]ert . Vnnd Im Achtunddreyss-
image-003 l.4 (continues): ...ss]igisten Jare /  [then a flourish/paraph "C"-like loop and a short flourished stroke at the right]
   -> joined: "[..]ert . Vnnd im Achtunddreyßigisten Jare /"
   Notes: the first word is cut at the left edge (ending "-ert" or "-ort"). The numeral word reads as "Achtund" + "drey" + a long-ß/ss ligature with a long descender + "igisten"; possibly "Achtunddreissigisten". "Jare" has a large flourished J. The date-line seems to continue above (the opening "...ert" probably ends a day or feast phrase). Year and day are not otherwise visible.
- Below the text: no further lines of writing, only the decorative flourishes (descending loops, an "S"-scroll). A faint looped stroke near the right edge of image-003 (~y 270-330) may be a paraph or the start of a notarial/scribal flourish, with tiny "a..."-like marks; not readable.

=== 2. 155v, later note (layer C), image-008 ===
image-008 l.~420: anzsluwang? / auzslnnangs? (reading very uncertain: minims plus long s or z, ends in g with a long descender and a superscript stroke)
image-008 l.~550: Hog? lohraimo? / Bog? lehrangno? (uncertain)
image-008 l.~650: D7? / Dy? (a capital D followed by a 7- or y-like stroke)
   Interpretation: probably an archival endorsement or summary note. I cannot read it with confidence.

=== 3. Older faded text (layer B) ===
3a. 155r: the image was rotated 90 degrees clockwise (enhanced copy of image-004) so the lines run left to right. In that orientation about 7 line traces show across image-004. Readable bits:
  rot-line ~1: [illegible] ... (fragment of letters at the torn corner)
  rot-line ~2: [illegible] ... "-cere"? / "-iam"? ...
  rot-line ~3: ... [illegible] ...
  rot-line ~4: ... m dirige? [hole] ab? omnes? ... (the clearest span: "dirige" fairly plausible; "ab om(n)es" doubtful)
  rot-line ~5: ... [illegible] ... "-is ... tue?" ...
  rot-line ~6: ... [hole] ... "-ui sa ea?" / "in eo e(st)?" ...
  rot-line ~7: ... [hole] ... "-ebigogi"? / "e(st) ego" ... m- ...
  In the same orientation, image-002 (bottom) shows the left/line-start parts of these lines; only "-us? ..."-type letter clusters are visible, with no words.
  The perpendicular rotation (counter-clockwise) gave mirror-like letter shapes, so I take clockwise as the reading direction. That is an inference.

3b. 155v (images 008-010, horizontal):
  image-008 l.~910: [red trace] [illegible] ... "-ns?" ... (about 4 letters before the central hole)
  image-008 l.~1045 / image-009 l.~180: d [hole] Exemp? / "exempl..."? ... [illegible]
  image-009 l.~315: ...p?ra? ... 4? ... [hole] ... "me cō..." / "rme c?" ...
  image-009 l.~455: "-a l?ui" ... "Tegna?"/"regnu?" ... [illegible] ... "-uas" / "-uat"
  image-009 l.~610: ... "a?" [hole] "d'i?" ... "lb?" ...
  image-009 l.~760: ... "g" ... [illegible]
  image-009 l.~915: ... "t? l?" ... [hole] "ru?gō?" ... "-ergo"? / "-e;gs"
  image-010 l.~160: "...mp; ⁊ de/da?" (the ⁊ / et-sign looks fairly secure)
  image-010 l.~320: "...-eat?"
  image-010 l.~455: "...ium? -uas" / "...nas"
  image-010 l.~610: "...ly ber?"
  image-010 l.~910: "...-rgs" / "-eg(us)?"
  Fragments on the tissue repair at the left edge of image-009 ("nes", "ec", "tu?") are on a pasted repair strip, possibly a scrap of another document. Not part of the leaf text.

UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Layer B is mostly lost to abrasion and flaking on both faces. Under enhancement only isolated letter groups appear and none of the above is reliable enough to support a source match. A multispectral/UV image would be needed.
- German line 1 is cut at the top edge. The left margin is trimmed, so line starts are lost ("5", "-ert").
- The reading of the later verso note is very uncertain.
- Suggested: UV or raking-light images of both faces for layer B. Also, if the charter's upper part survives on an adjacent fragment, that would give context for the dating line.
